Critical Edge Cases and Architectural Challenges

Deploying automated classification at scale across thousands of heterogeneous files reveals

significant technical hurdles that challenge both paradigms:

• CJK Multi-Byte Repositories: Fonts containing tens of thousands of ideographic

glyphs cannot fit legibly onto a single standard 16:9 grid without severe downscaling,

leading to loss of fine structural detail for CNN encoders.

• Variable Fonts (.ttf/.otf with ‘fvar‘ tables): Modern variable fonts encode

an axis continuum of weight, width, and slant within a single file. Deterministic

parsers must extract multi-instance bounding boxes, while AI models must decide

which master instance(s) to render for evaluation.

• Ornaments, Dingbats, and Symbol Fonts: Fonts lacking standard Latin alphabetic characters yield structural tensors that break standard text-classification

Proposed Hybrid Methodology

To maximize accuracy while controlling computational overhead, we propose a hybrid

dual-pipeline architecture:

1. Fast Deterministic Filtering: Initial ingestion passes files through ‘fontTools‘

to validate structural integrity, extract clean metadata, and filter out corrupted or

non-text symbol files.

2. Targeted Neural Rendering: Flagged or ambiguous fonts, along with a representative sample, are rendered into monochrome 16:9 frames and processed via CNN

inference.

3. Unified Latent Sequencing: Combined metrics dictate the optimized sorting

topology for downstream publishing and cinematic frame generation.

The development of the MEDUSA platform started in 2013. Back then, this kind of

cloud-based solutions was not common. Today, however, there is a clear trend in the

healthcare industry towards the usage of cloud computing, collaboration, and automated analyses of medical data. In addition, when dealing with processing of medical

data constrained by the requirements of acute care situations, a lot of benefits can be

derived from the use of cloud computing: scalability, pay-per-use model, high performance computing capabilities, remote access, etc.

SIMT Warp Divergence and Bus Locality

Modern discrete and integrated GPUs schedule fragment

shaders across Single Instruction, Multiple Threads (SIMT)

execution units [7]. Escape-time fractal evaluation exhibits

inherent control-flow divergence: pixels exterior to the

a warp.

parameter updates restricted to compact uniform blocks

fragment shaders, the monolithic PWA minimizes host-todevice bus traffic.

FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The invention relates to the field of document processing, and more specifically to document processing allowing to query a document retrieval system. More specifically, the invention relates a computer-implemented method, system and computer program for generating a query representation of an electronic query document. The invention also relates to a computer-implemented method, system and computer program for querying a

epresentation of an electronic query document. The invention also relates to a computer-implemented method, system and computer program for querying a document retrieval system, using the query representation of the electronic query document to retrieve relevant documents or information related to such documents. The invention further relates to a computer-implemented method, system and computer program for clustering similar documents in a set of electronic documents.

Herein, a document retrieval system is any system allowing to query an index of documents with one or more word sequences (including exact phrases) and returning results ranked by relevance. The word sequences may be linked by Boolean operators, and results may be provided with a relevance score. Examples of documents retrieval systems are systems based on Lucene, Oracle Database or SQL server.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION Ever since people and organizations have had to deal with massive quantities of electronic documents, there are attempts to use smart, cognitive methods to identify and select documents of relevance out of a large number, e.g. millions, of candidate documents. In such methods for finding relevant documents, a specific document, referred to as a reference document or a query document, may be used as a basis for setting up a query for similar, comparable documents. The query document is processed to generate some form of representation of its content, sometimes called a profile or fingerprint.

Several approaches exist to generate a query from a query document. As documents in general mostly contain text, and as texts are made of words, all approaches include some form of text analysis to identify meaningful units of text deemed relevant for building the query. Some approaches are limited to identifying key phrases (a phrase being a plurality of words), whereas others mention phrases as just one of the types of units to consider, next to single words and other entities.

2. Related Work and Theoretical Foundations

2.1 Client-Side Compute and WebGL Evolution

The transition of web browsers from simple document viewers to robust application runtimes has been extensively documented in systems literature [4]. Early web-based visualization frameworks depended heavily on CPU-bound rasterization, severely limiting frame rates when rendering complex mathematical objects. The introduction of WebGL 2.0 bridged this gap by providing direct access to the OpenGL ES 3.0 graphics pipeline, enabling fragment-shader-driven parallel execution across available GPU hardware [8].

However, unlike native CUDA environments where memory pointers can be manipulated directly within unified address spaces, WebGL operates within a strictly typed, memory-isolated sandbox. Previous attempts to simulate deep-zoom fractals within browser environments succumbed to floating-point precision degradation beyond single-precision IEEE 754 limits ($\sim 7$ decimal digits) or suffered catastrophic performance drops when utilizing arbitrary-precision software emulation libraries [5, 6, 9].

2.2 GPU Execution Paradigms and Memory Bandwidth

Modern discrete graphics accelerators, such as NVIDIA architectures utilizing the CUDA programming model, optimize execution through Single Instruction, Multiple Threads (SIMT) streaming multiprocessors (SMs) [3, 7]. While highly efficient for regular matrix operations, recursive ray-marching and fractal escape-time algorithms introduce severe warp divergence. Threads evaluating points that diverge rapidly terminate execution early, while threads tracking deep boundaries execute maximum iterations, serializing execution blocks within the warp.

Rendering recursive mathematical boundaries introduces severe spatial aliasing. Traditional full-scene multi-sampling anti-aliasing (MSAA) multiplies fill-rate costs linearly. 5. Discussion and Limitations

While the monolithic PWA architecture achieves unprecedented client-side compute density, certain limitations remain. First, browser-level security policies and memory allocation caps can restrict deep recursion buffers on constrained mobile devices. Second, Safari's WebGL implementation exhibits minor shader compilation variances compared to ANGLE on Chromium-based browsers, requiring explicit extension handling. Finally, extremely deep orbits ($\log_{10} > 30$) require arbitrary precision big-float CPU pre-calculation passes, introducing occasional frame pacing jitter.

6. Conclusion and Future Horizons

In this paper, we have demonstrated that complex, high-entropy scientific simulations and fractal universe renderers need not rely on heavy native binaries. By synthesizing monolithic PWA delivery, analytic perturbation theory, and optimized sub-pixel blur kernels, we have established a robust paradigm that matches native hardware performance while ensuring complete reproducibility. Future work will extend this architecture to decentralized peer-to-peer WebRTC compute swarms and investigate WebGPU compute shader pipelines for higher-dimensional quaternion topologies.
